lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé does not make its product or operations-strategy direction explicit.
items.because: The mix of mechanics, logistics, product, and consulting makes the reader work to understand your target role.

items.says: Rebalance or reorder the sections for the target role.
items.because: Product-relevant work appears after the current diesel-mechanic role, which can suggest a move away from product.

items.says: Consider a specific summary connecting your training, experience, and target role.
items.because: A targeted summary could keep the roles from appearing unrelated.

items.says: Audit metrics throughout for periods, scope, attribution, and causal support.
items.because: Imprecise metrics can undermine otherwise strong achievements.

items.says: Add a target-position descriptor near the contact information.
items.because: The contact line gives no indication of your professional focus.

items.says: Check and replace the apparent placeholder professional-profile URL.
items.because: The URL looks like a generic website rather than a LinkedIn profile.

items.says: Consider adding location or work authorization if relevant.
Make clear whether the MBA is completed.
items.because: A date range without a completion indicator can create uncertainty.

items.says: Add a strong, relevant concentration, course, leadership role, award, or distinction if available.
items.because: The current format does not explain how the MBA supports the target role.

items.says: Remove the bachelor’s-degree location if space is needed.
items.because: The degree is no longer the primary selling point.

items.says: Contextualize why the current diesel-mechanic role belongs in a product or operations application.
items.because: A recruiter may otherwise assume you are changing direction away from product or business roles.

items.says: Consider giving the mechanic role less space unless hands-on operations are relevant to the target role.
items.because: It should not compete with the product narrative.

items.says: Clarify the scale and your ownership of the rebuild work.
items.because: The mechanical work is not naturally connected to product or business operations.

items.says: Explain the operational significance of keeping dry-dock time under five days.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether that is an improvement, a required standard, or normal duration.

items.says: Confirm that under five days per job was repeatable rather than an isolated best case.
Consider whether the hydraulic-winch bullet is worth keeping for the target roles.
items.because: It is less relevant to product roles than nearly every other bullet.

items.says: Emphasize its operational, compliance, asset-management, or documentation dimension.
items.because: As written, it primarily lists maintenance responsibilities.

items.says: Add the scale or consequence of the maintenance and inspection work.
items.because: The bullet shows no measurable result, improvement, or scope.

items.says: Give Crestline more emphasis for product-operations or operations-strategy roles.
items.because: It is one of the strongest sections for those roles.

items.says: Add the scale of the carrier scorecards.
items.because: The reader cannot see how many carriers, shipments, managers, regions, or metrics they covered.

items.says: Explain what decisions or business changes the scorecards enabled.
items.because: Owning the reporting and meeting shows responsibility but not value.

items.says: Say whether you built, improved, or merely administered the reporting process.
items.because: The bullet currently reads as administrative rather than showing analytical ownership.

items.says: Add the pick-error baseline or operational consequence.
items.because: The reduction has more context with error volume, customer impact, cost, or returns.

items.says: Clarify your role relative to the floor supervisors.
items.because: The bullet does not separate your analysis, design, implementation, and training contributions.

items.says: Specify the period over which the 30% reduction was measured.
items.because: A defined period makes the percentage reduction more credible.

items.says: Make the forecast’s size and business importance clearer.
Clarify whether you created the consensus method or facilitated its adoption.
items.because: The distinction matters to the level of ownership claimed.

items.says: Specify the forecast horizon or error metric if appropriate.
items.because: An analytically rigorous audience may need the metric defined.

items.says: Separate or clarify the rollout, procedures, training, and vendor-management responsibilities.
items.because: Several achievements in one long sentence can obscure the strongest one.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 driver hours saved annually were calculated.
Clarify your level of ownership in the vendor negotiation.
items.because: The boundaries between operational work and commercial negotiation should be clear.

items.says: Add the financial, capacity, or service impact of the hours saved if available.
Reorder and consolidate the internship bullets into fewer distinct workstreams.
items.because: Six overlapping bullets for a ten-week internship can look repetitive or inflated.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the onboarding redesign.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish discovery, design, coordination, and launch work.

items.says: Check whether the before-and-after onboarding cohorts were comparable.
items.because: The wording implies the redesign caused the entire improvement.

items.says: Consider including an activation, support, or retention outcome if available.
Clarify that the conversion change is in percentage points rather than a relative percent increase.
items.because: Product and growth interviewers will probe the interpretation of the result.

items.says: Verify the test’s measurement details and state statistical significance if known.
items.because: The test design and interpretation are likely to receive scrutiny.

items.says: Define whether all merchants means the pilot region or the entire merchant base.
items.because: The rollout scope is unclear.

items.says: Do not imply the wider rollout produced the same lift unless it was measured.
Show the roadmap decision or outcome that resulted from RICE prioritization.
items.because: Naming the framework alone shows familiarity, not product judgment.

items.says: Add the number of features, stakeholders, or choices involved if available.
Clarify whether the support-ticket definition of Reach was an intentional adaptation.
items.because: Otherwise it may look like a misunderstanding of RICE.

items.says: Distinguish the chargeback roadmap work from the preceding RICE bullet.
items.because: Both bullets appear to describe roadmap prioritization.

items.says: Clarify whether you recommended, influenced, or made the final priority decision.
items.because: Set the next quarter’s roadmap priority may sound too absolute for an intern.

items.says: Add the business outcome of the roadmap choice.
items.because: The bullet does not say whether an investment was approved, a feature shipped, or losses were expected to fall.

items.says: Make the connection between research, loss analysis, and the roadmap choice explicit.
Remove or consolidate this checkout-test bullet with the earlier conversion bullet.
items.because: It largely duplicates the same experiment without adding a new business result.

items.says: Check the unit of analysis and interpretation of the reported customer effect.
items.because: The technical explanation invites methodological questions.

items.says: Clarify whether session-level randomization caused exposure or repeat-user concerns.
Clarify whether you presented independently or as part of a team.
items.because: The bullet does not establish your personal contribution.

items.says: Identify what leadership’s approval enabled.
Confirm that leadership formally funded, rather than merely approved, the rollout.
items.because: Funded may overstate the decision if no budget was allocated.

items.says: Clarify the app’s operating context and whether you, a team, or an external developer built it.
items.because: A recruiter needs to understand the student venture’s legitimacy and operating scale.

items.says: Define whether 3,100 students were the addressable audience, registered users, or users reached.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the product served them or was merely available to them.

items.says: Explain your role in the launch and adoption.
Support the claim that the food would otherwise have been thrown away.
items.because: The food-waste counterfactual depends on how the food was tracked.

items.says: Mention the type of partner involvement if there were partner organizations.
The stated 150% weekly-active-user increase is miscalculated.
items.because: An increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%.

items.says: Add the period over which weekly active users increased.
Confirm weekly active users were measured consistently before and after the change.
Clarify whether the interviews led directly to reminders or merely informed the decision.
items.because: Interviews do not by themselves prove reminders caused the full increase.

items.says: The 20% fill-rate increase uses the wrong mathematical phrasing.
items.because: Moving from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, or about 27% relative growth.

items.says: Add the period and number of pickup slots or shifts.
Explain your role in designing and implementing the volunteer shift system.
Position the result intentionally as product work, operations work, or both.
items.because: It shows product work extending beyond software into service operations.

items.says: Clarify whether the $2.4M is modeled, validated, or realized savings.
items.because: The distinction matters for credibility.

items.says: Identify the main inputs to the savings model if space permits.
Specify whether you built the model or led the team that built it.
Add a measurable result from the intake-form changes.
items.because: Adopted is a vague outcome that does not show what improved.

items.says: Clarify whether the form work was part of the scheduling recommendation or a separate workstream.
Explain your role in mapping, redesign, and adoption.
items.because: The bullet uses a passive process description.

items.says: Consider removing the bullet if no outcome can be added and space is tight.
items.because: As written, it is a process description with a weak outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether you or the full team presented the recommendation.
Consolidate the pilot-approval outcome with the earlier practicum bullet.
items.because: Both bullets use the same client approval as evidence of impact.

items.says: Add defensible analytical or operational capabilities demonstrated elsewhere.
items.because: The four listed skills undersell the operations, forecasting, and cross-functional experience.

items.says: Distinguish methods you used directly from those you merely studied.
items.because: Every listed skill should be supportable in an interview.

items.says: Show the level of ownership behind roadmapping.
items.because: The skill should not imply more authority than the experience demonstrates.

items.says: Add other relevant tools only if you have used them meaningfully.
items.because: The current tools list is thin for product and analytics roles.

items.says: Show the specific Excel work in an experience bullet.
items.because: The generic tool name does not convey your proficiency.

items.says: Support Jira and Amplitude with concrete uses in the experience section.
items.because: The résumé does not show where or how you used them.
